cells.reason: The anchor is the California drinking-water MCL for hexavalent chromium, 0.010 mg/L for community and nontransient-noncommunity public water systems (scope 'drinking water'; regulation page: 'This is a drinking-water standard, not a food limit' and 'should not be compared directly to a food-occurrence concentration'), while the cell is an as-sold dried-food content cell, so criterion (b) fails: a water row is not a food-content row and the face-value transfer of 10 ug/L to 10 ug/kg of dried seaweed is supported by no instrument. The register holds no food-content Cr-VI sovereign row anywhere (the remaining Cr-VI rows are AU/CA water, EU toy migration, REACH textiles and leather, RoHS, tattoo ink and fertiliser), so no same-basis read-across exists; the defensible treatment is a subsumed cell bounded by the parent total-chromium cell (Cr-VI <= Cr-total 2000 as sold) or a disclosed baseline screen, not a firm 10 ug/kg.
